name: Superficial Epidermolytic Ichthyosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Superficial Epidermolytic Ichthyosis

criteria.description: Presence of superficial blistering and mild ichthyosis predominantly on flexural areas, often with a history of blistering at birth or early infancy
Histological evidence of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis with vacuolar degeneration of the upper epidermis and coarse keratohyalin granules
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the KRT2 gene
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern or positive family history of similar skin findings

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features plus either histopathological confirmation or identification of a pathogenic KRT2 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is confirmatory; histopathology is supportive but essential in absence of genetic data.

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermolytic hyperkeratosis with vacuolar degeneration of upper epidermis
other: Clinical observation of superficial blistering and scaling
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: More severe blistering and hyperkeratosis involving deeper epidermis
Mutations in KRT1 or KRT10 genes
Onset typically at birth with widespread involvement
Fine scaling predominantly on extensor surfaces

redFlags: Signs of systemic infection or sepsis
references: Hohl D, et al. Superficial epidermolytic ichthyosis: clinical, histological, and molecular findings. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2006.
